title: Synergy Overflow
pitch: You are the founder of an invented company pitching buzzword cards to a very gullible board: some add headcount, some add hype, some multiply it by synergy, and a few raise it to a power called disruption. Targets grow like an idle game's cost curve, order matters, and by quarter twenty the numbers have names nobody learned, until the page finally overflows into a deliberate, theatrical NaN-e-Inf board meeting. The joke is the deadpan corporate voice, the payoff is watching the maths run out of numbers.
whyNow: Timeless satire of numbers-go-up design and corporate buzzword inflation; it also fills the owed humor slot with a real mechanic rather than a one-liner.

research.summary: Incremental and idle games rest on a simple recipe: costs rise exponentially (a growth factor of 1.15 per purchase is the convention popularised by one famous clicker, per an analysis paper and a developer write-up) while income rises more slowly, so designers tune payback time and reset with prestige. The deckbuilder community has a famous joke ending: scores that exceed double precision display as a garbled overflow word, with an endless-mode wall and mods that push the cap far higher. That pairing, exponential targets plus an overflow punchline, is a real mechanic with a built-in comedic ending. The satire targets generic corporate speak with an invented company; no real firms or people.

facts.claim: A cost growth factor of 1.15 per purchase is a common idle-game convention, cited for one famous clicker (as of 2026-10-12).
In the inspiration game, scores beyond the floating-point limit show as an overflow state nicknamed naneinf, discussed by an event write-up, a forum thread and a mod description (as of 2026-10-12).

The double-precision limit is about 1.8 times 10 to the 308; one forum estimate puts the overflow near that figure. The page will compute this itself in the browser and label the forum figure as reported.
A 2026 live event write-up reports a player reaching the overflow state in a run of about 1 hour 16 minutes (reported by one source, unverified).

inspirations: the overflow joke ending of deckbuilder endless modes

design.coreLoop: Each quarter the board sets a target; you draw five buzzword cards, play up to four in an order you choose, and the score tree runs in front of you with a deadpan commentary line per card. Beat the target to get a perk card for the deck or restructure (prestige) to reset with a permanent multiplier. It stays interesting because order, exponent cards and a rising deck-thinning decision make each draw a small optimisation, and because the ending is a joke worth reaching.
sophisticationHooks: Log-space big-number type (mantissa plus exponent) with named-number formatting beyond the 15-digit double limit
Target curve built from a tunable growth factor and payback-time check so a run lasts about 25 quarters
Optional chief-of-staff hint that brute-forces card orders and shows the best order score without revealing the card choice
Scripted overflow finale: the display glitches into NaN-e-Inf, the board applauds, and the run ends with a shareable certificate
design.scopeForOneDay: Built: card pool of about 30 invented buzzword cards, run loop with seeded draws, big-number class with tests, commentary lines, overflow finale, share string, about panel, light and dark, reduced motion. Cut: sound, meta-progression beyond one prestige layer, more than one company.
risks: Humor must land: commentary lines need a writing pass and generic invented company names only, no real firms, brands or people
Looks like an idle toy; mitigate with decisions every turn and a defined ending
Overlap with the carried-over Breaking Changes humor idea is thematic only (corporate voice), so the mechanic and subject are different
Floating-point claims: the page states the double limit as computed in-browser and labels forum figures as reported
Event write-up detail (run time) is from one result and stays unverified
